principle: Both reds were taken against SHIPPED code at the baseline commit, before any implementation line existed in the worktree. R2 is a live browser failure at the real boundary, not a unit-level restatement.

R1.name: the lifecycle-pack selector does not exist
R1.provesWhat: The ladder has no lifecycle group to run, so no lifecycle row can be gated by CI today.
R1.predictionCorrection: The admission receipt predicted exit 3 NOT_IMPLEMENTED. The observed exit is 2 UNKNOWN_GROUP, because `lifecycle-pack` is absent from GROUP_CATALOG entirely rather than reserved-without-a-spec: buildRunPlan throws UNKNOWN_GROUP at scripts/qc/gm-two-player-campaign-core.cjs:44 before the NOT_IMPLEMENTED branch at :172 is reachable, and runCli maps UNKNOWN_GROUP to 2 at :257-261. The admission receipt said the exact code would be captured rather than predicted; this is that capture.

R2.name: shipped code does not assert any lifecycle state unconditionally

R2.provesWhat: On baseline 7489e311f the ONLY reads of data-testid="tactical-lifecycle-state" anywhere in e2e/ are (a) this tautological guard, which asserts a string against a pattern it has already been tested against and therefore can never fail, and (b) the disjunctive `^(live|finalized)$` command-gating poll at the same file :876-881. When the guard is removed the shipped banner reports `finalized` for a viewer whose delivery cursor is provably frozen at the unacked cap - so not one of the letter's nine states is pinned by any live row, and the one state the suite does observe is the converged-adjacent one.
R2.strongerThanPredicted: The admission receipt predicted the banner would read `live`. It read `finalized`, which is the same class of finding (a converged posture on an isolated viewer) with a sharper edge: `finalized` is one of the two states carrying commandsEnabled: true (src/lib/multiplayer/tacticalLifecycleState.ts:155), so the shipped surface was telling a cursor-frozen viewer that commands were enabled.
R2.notAClaim: This red is evidence about ASSERTION COVERAGE, not a product defect report. Whether `finalized` is the correct posture for an unacked-capped viewer is E2E-14's question and belongs to its own row; U1c does not rule on it and does not change that row. The residual is named in the local receipt.

environmentProvenByR2.note: R2 doubles as the environment proof for stage 3: the production build served through `node server.js` booted, three contexts joined, and the server log shows `intent dispatched ... intent=GoProne` and `intent=AdvancePhase`, which is the wire-level intent lever the lifecycle row's `sealed` state depends on.

junctionHydrateRefusal.message: {"ok": false, "error": "Unsafe hydration destination (runtime loader tsx) contains a symlink or junction: .next\\standalone\\node_modules", "hint": "Run npm run build first so .next/standalone/server.js exists, then hydrate the standalone multiplayer server."}
junctionHydrateRefusal.whyNotBlocking: The ladder runner launches `node server.js` (scripts/qc/gm-two-player-campaign-core.cjs:212-215), and server.js only takes the standalone path when server.next-config.json exists beside it (server.js:35-46, `isStandaloneRuntime`). That file is absent in this worktree, so server.js boots the ordinary Next production server from .next/ and never reads the unhydrated .next/standalone/node_modules. R2 booting and running a full three-context row is the live proof.
